openingTemplate: {{who}} makes a remark about {{subject}} in front of {{audience}}. It is delivered lightly, and it is not the first time.

escalations.template:
You said: "{{answer}}"

They double down, and this time someone else laughs along.
Afterwards they ask, apparently sincerely, whether you are alright. Same answer?

referenceAnswer: The remark only cuts if I agree that it counts, and the agreement is mine to withhold. If the pattern is worth raising it is worth raising privately and without heat, not as a counterpunch in front of an audience.
exemplars: It lands because part of me agrees with it. That is mine to look at, not theirs to fix.

openingTemplate: You are waiting to hear about {{thing}}. It has been {{duration}}. You have checked {{channel}} more times today than you would admit to.

thing: whether they want a second conversation

escalations.template:
You said: "{{answer}}"

Someone mentions, casually, that they think a decision was made last week.
Still nothing by Friday evening. The weekend is now in front of you. Same answer?

referenceAnswer: My part is finished, and the outcome sits with people on a timeline I cannot see. One follow-up is reasonable. After that the checking is not diligence, it is paying the anxiety in instalments.
exemplars: The part that was mine is done. Continuing to work on it is just wanting, louder.

openingTemplate: {{who}} sends you {{message}}. Nothing else. You have now read it {{count}} times.

message: a full stop and nothing else
count: more than you want to say

escalations.template:
You said: "{{answer}}"

They come online, stay online for a while, and do not message.
The next morning they are completely normal, as if nothing happened. Same answer?

referenceAnswer: A short message arrived. Everything I have felt since is a reading I authored in about two seconds. I can ask plainly, once, or I can let it be unresolved, but I do not have to defend myself against something nobody has said.
exemplars: I wrote the subtext myself and then got upset at my own draft.

openingTemplate: You sit down to {{task}}. Within {{window}}, without deciding to, you are {{escape}}.

window: the time it takes to open the file

escalations.template:
You said: "{{answer}}"

You come back, start properly, and the work gets hard in a small specific way. The reach happens again.
An hour gone. You have produced one paragraph you do not like. Same answer?

referenceAnswer: The reach is timed to the difficulty, not to the clock, which makes it an escape rather than a habit. The gap I am training is the ninety seconds after it gets hard.
exemplars: It happens exactly when the work gets uncomfortable. That timing is the whole tell.

openingTemplate: You have lost {{amount}}. It is {{time}} and there is a strong pull to write off {{scope}}.
instinctOptions: Work late to make it up

escalations.template:
You said: "{{answer}}"

You start, and the thought arrives that there is not enough time left to do it properly anyway.
You get about an hour of real work done. Half the day used, half not. Same answer?

referenceAnswer: Losing the morning is the event. That the day is ruined is a judgment I added, and it is the one that turns four lost hours into nine. What is left does not have to redeem what is gone.
exemplars: The judgment costs more than the event did. That is almost always where it goes wrong.

openingTemplate: Day {{day}}. You said you would {{commitment}} and today you did not. {{context}}

context: Nothing dramatic happened. You just did not.
There was a reason, and it was not a good one.
You noticed yourself deciding, and did it anyway.

escalations.template:
You said: "{{answer}}"

The next day you miss it again, and this time the missing was easier.
You catch yourself thinking that you never stick to anything. Same answer?

referenceAnswer: A missed day is a missed day, not a verdict on my character. The story I am about to build out of it is the part that does real damage, because that story does the work of making itself true.
exemplars: Broken streaks are data, not identity. The story afterwards is what actually ends things.

openingTemplate: You could {{shortcut}} and {{consequence}}. It would save you {{saving}}.

shortcut: say it is done when it is nearly done
leave out the part that complicates it
consequence: it would almost certainly never surface

escalations.template:
You said: "{{answer}}"

You remember you have done this before, more than once, and nothing came of it then either.
It goes through. Nobody notices, exactly as predicted. Same answer?

referenceAnswer: Nobody knowing is what makes this the actual test rather than a hypothetical one. The corner costs a day. The other thing costs a small permanent adjustment to what I am willing to do, and those compound quietly.
exemplars: Having got away with it before is not reassurance. It is the drift I should be watching.

openingTemplate: A decision goes against you and the reasoning is {{quality}}. {{who}} got the thing instead.

quality: based on something that is not true
who: Someone who has been there longer

instinctOptions: Make the case it was wrong
Let it change how you work

escalations.template:
You said: "{{answer}}"

You learn the decision was largely made before the process started.
Someone asks how you are taking it. You hear yourself being generous, and you are not sure you mean it. Same answer?

referenceAnswer: It can be genuinely unfair and still not be mine. Asking for the reasoning is column one and worth doing once. Relitigating it afterwards means I can win the argument completely and remain exactly where I am.
exemplars: Ask once, plainly, then stop. Being right about it does not move me an inch.
